author: "The elder" (1:1), who does not give his name. Early Christian tradition identifies him as John the apostle, who also wrote the Gospel of John and 1 John; the letter's wording closely matches 1 John.
recipients: "The elect lady and her children" (1:1). This may be a Christian woman and her family, or a figurative name for a local church and its members; the letter itself does not say which. It closes with greetings from "the children of thy elect sister" (1:13).

date.traditional: About AD 85-95, late in John's life, around the same time as 1 John.
date.scholarly: Most scholars also place it in the late first century. Some think "the elder" was a church leader other than the apostle.

writtenFrom: Not stated. Early tradition places John's last years in Ephesus.
destination: Not stated: a church or household the elder knew and hoped to visit soon (1:12), likely in the province of Asia.
purpose: To urge the readers to keep walking in truth and in love, which means walking after God's commandments (1:4-6), and to warn them not to welcome or support travelling teachers who deny that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh (1:7-11).
setting: Christian teachers travelled between churches and depended on believers to house them. Some who had gone out from the churches taught that Jesus Christ had not come in the flesh (compare 1 John 2:19, 4:1-3). Domitian was emperor (AD 81-96).

outline.title: Walk in truth and love one another

themes: Love is walking after God's commandments (1:6).
Jesus Christ has come in the flesh; denying it is the mark of a deceiver (1:7).
Hospitality must not become support for false teaching (1:10-11).
basis: From the letter's own text, compared with 1 John; authorship and dating views summarized from standard introductions.
